param_input_item.param_description: 0 (default) for Ai, 1 for the derivative of Ai, 2 for Bi, 3 for the derivative of Bi.
0 (default) or 1 to return the scaled values.

description.p: airy(K, Z) computes the Airy function Ai (K = 0), its derivative (K = 1), the Airy function Bi (K = 2) or its derivative (K = 3) for each element of Z. airy(Z) returns Ai(Z). Ai and Bi are solutions of the Airy equation:
With scale = 1, Ai and its derivative are multiplied by exp(2/3 * Z.^(3/2)), Bi and its derivative by exp(-abs(real(2/3 * Z.^(3/2)))).
The result is single when an input is single, and real when every imaginary part is zero.
Values are computed with a C++ port of the Amos algorithms, for any real order and any complex argument.

xmldoc.bibliography: D. E. Amos, Algorithm 644: A portable package for Bessel functions of a complex argument and nonnegative order, ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software, 12 (1986), pp. 265-273.
